Before jumping into the different meanings, here's the thread that connects all of them: a slur always involves something being blurred, smeared, or dragged in a way that causes damage or loss of clarity — whether it's someone's reputation, a group's dignity, or the clarity of sounds in speech or music. Keep that idea in mind as you read through the meanings below.
Meaning 1: An Offensive Word or Statement (the most common meaning)

This is the meaning most people encounter most often. A slur is a word, phrase, or remark that attacks or degrades a person or a group of people — usually based on something about their identity, such as their race, religion, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, or disability.

A slur doesn't just criticize someone. It dehumanizes them. It reduces an entire group of people to a stereotype, treating their identity as something shameful or inferior. This is what makes slurs different from ordinary insults. A regular insult attacks what someone did. A slur attacks what someone is.

For example: A racial slur is a word used to demean someone because of their race. Such words carry a long history of hatred and discrimination, which is a big part of why they cause such deep harm.

You'll often hear the phrase "hurling a slur" or "using a slur", which captures how these words are thrown at people like weapons.

A few important points to understand the full picture:

  • Context matters enormously. Some communities have reclaimed slurs that were once used against them, using the words among themselves in a way that strips the hatred out of them. However, the same word used by an outsider, or used with hostile intent, remains a slur in the harmful sense.
  • A slur doesn't have to be a single word. It can be a phrase or remark that implies inferiority or contempt toward a group.
  • Slurs cause real harm. Research consistently shows that being targeted by slurs causes psychological distress, feelings of exclusion, and lasting emotional damage. This is why they are treated as a serious matter in law, workplace policy, and social life.
Meaning 2: A Stain on Someone's Reputation

In a more formal or old-fashioned sense, a slur is a damaging claim or suggestion made against a person's character or reputation, often one that is unfair or unproven.

For example: "The accusation was a slur on his reputation that he never fully recovered from."

Think of it like a muddy smear on a clean surface. Even after you wipe it away, a trace often remains. That's what a reputational slur does — it leaves a mark of suspicion or shame on how others perceive a person. This meaning overlaps closely with Meaning 1, but it is broader because it doesn't have to involve identity-based hatred. It can simply be a false or malicious claim that damages how someone is seen publicly.
Meaning 3: A Curved Mark in Written Music

This meaning is completely unrelated to insults. In the world of music, a slur is a curved line drawn above or below a group of notes in written music (sheet music). It tells the performer to play or sing those notes smoothly and connected, flowing from one note to the next without any gap or break between them. This style of playing is called legato (a term from Italian meaning "tied together").

For example: A singer seeing a slur over five notes knows to sing those five notes in one smooth, unbroken breath, almost melting one into the next.

A slur is different from a tie, which is a similar-looking curved line but only connects two notes of the same pitch, simply extending the duration of that one note. A slur, by contrast, connects notes of different pitches and is purely an instruction about smoothness and connection.
Meaning 4: A Blurring of Sounds in Speech

A slur can also refer to the act or result of running speech sounds together in a way that makes words unclear or hard to understand. When someone speaks very quickly, is extremely tired, or is under the influence of alcohol or certain medications, their words may lose their sharp edges and blur into each other. The resulting unclear, mushy speech can itself be called a slur — or the unclear sounds are said to be "slurred."

For example: "His speech came out as a slur — nobody could make out what he was saying."
How All the Meanings Fit Together

Now you can see why that one core idea — smearing, blurring, dragging — holds all these meanings together.

  • An offensive slur smears a person's dignity or identity.
  • A reputational slur smears a person's good name.
  • A musical slur drags notes together in a smooth, connected flow.
  • A speech slur drags sounds together until they lose their clarity.

The word wears different clothes in different contexts, but the same underlying sense runs through all of them.
